title: Reverting a change, product by product: what a write does, how to undo it, and what cannot be undone

prose.text: Reversibility depends on the product. ZIA stages writes until they are activated [[zia.api.activation:saved-not-live]], and the captured specifications show no activation call for the other products [[shared.activation:no-other-gate]].

rows: ZIA
Staged until activated [[zia.api.activation:saved-not-live]]. A session end activates pending changes [[zia.terraform.activation-methods:session-end-autoactivation]].
Re-write the original values before the session ends. Once activated, a change cannot be reverted [[shared.oneapi.write-practices:activation-zia-cbc]].
Cloud & Branch Connector
Staged until activated, and a forced activation route exists [[cloud-connector.api.activation-wire:python-force-flag]].
Revert staged changes as for ZIA. What forced activation does beyond a normal activation is open [[cloud-connector.api.activation-wire:force-semantics]].
ZPA
No activation call in the captured specifications. Whether a write is live at once is open [[zpa.api.activation:write-takes-effect]].
Snapshot the resource and re-write the snapshot [[shared.oneapi.write-practices:fetch-before-update]].
Client Connector
App profile changes download on logout or restart [[zcc.app-profiles.propagation:download-on-relogin]].
Re-write the profile. Forwarding profile and trusted network timing is open {{gap:checkin-timing}}.
ZIdentity
No activation call in the captured specifications [[shared.activation:no-other-gate]].
Snapshot first. A deleted API client cannot be recovered [[zidentity.api-clients:delete-unrecoverable]].
Workflow Automation (ZWA)
Config changes apply to the next DLP incident. In-flight incidents keep their workflow {{gap:zwa-workflow-timing}}.
Snapshot the configuration before a change.
AI Guard
Configuration resources are reached through OneAPI [[ai-security.ai-guard.admin-api:python-oneapi]].

The captured action routes are enable, disable and referential-check [[ai-security.ai-guard.admin-api:colon-action-routes]]. Whether the live API accepts them is open [[ai-security.ai-guard.admin-api:live-acceptance]].
Risk360, ZMS and Deception
Risk360 has no client surface [[risk360.overview:no-client-surface]], and the ZMS API is read-only [[zms.api:clients-read-only]]. Deception {{gap:deception-rollback}}.
No verified SDK or Terraform rollback path. Use the product's own reference boundary.

prose.text: The Python client attribute client.zbi is Business Insights, not Zero Trust Browser [[shared.terminology.product-names:zbi-is-business-insights]].

items.text: A provisioning key at maximum usage cannot deploy more connectors, though its maximum can be edited [[zpa.app-connectors.provisioning-keys:exhausted-key-blocks-deploy]].
Enrollment certificate validity and renewal are open [[zpa.app-connectors.enrollment:certificate-validity-window]].
Whether a deleted resource can be restored is open {{gap:deleted-recreated-id}}.
Whether streamed LSS logs can be recovered from Zscaler is open {{gap:lss-streamed-logs}}.
Whether blocked DLP content is delivered when its rule is reverted is open {{gap:dlp-blocked-content}}.

checks.do: Before a risky ZIA change, read the current objects and keep them: a revert is a re-write of the original values before the session ends.
Start a ZIA change only when the activation status reads ACTIVE.
Re-read a staged value before activating. If it is wrong, re-write the original, because a change cannot be reverted once activated.
Stage related changes together and activate them as one step, because a queued activation waits on other admins' changes.
Assume another admin or automation can activate your staged revert. Whether activation is per admin is open.
Do not rely on discarding pending ZIA changes. Whether an API can do that without activating is open.
After activation, a counter-change can be staged and activated, but it does not undo the period in which the first change was live.
For ZPA, snapshot the segment before the change and re-write the snapshot to revert. Whether a write is live at once is open, so treat the window as live.
When restoring a ZPA application segment, pass its port forms and omit clientless_app_ids for a standard segment. An update clears any port form not passed.
For ZIdentity, snapshot the API client before a change. A deleted API client cannot be recovered.
For Client Connector app profiles, expect a change on the device at logout or restart. The timing for forwarding profiles and trusted networks is open.
For AI Guard, validate the enable and disable routes on the tenant before relying on them for rollback. The live API is not captured.
Do not treat Cloud & Branch Connector forced activation as a rollback: what it does beyond a normal activation is open.
Do not assume a deleted resource can be restored. Recreating it gives a new ID, so references to the old ID need rewiring.
Do not expect a provisioning key at maximum usage to deploy more connectors. Its maximum can be edited.
Plan enrollment certificate renewal from the captured validity window, which is open.
Treat streamed LSS logs and DLP-blocked content as unrecoverable until a source says otherwise.
Schedule a risky ZPA change for a maintenance window, since the write may take effect at once.
For Risk360, ZMS and Deception, use the product's own reference boundary: there is no verified SDK or Terraform rollback path.

checkin-timing.title: When Client Connector forwarding-profile and trusted-network changes reach a device
checkin-timing.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Forwarding Profile and Trusted Network changes apply when the agent next checks in.' The captured help covers app-profile downloads on logout or restart (zcc.app-profiles.propagation:download-on-relogin) and a check-in for a modified app profile, not these two settings.

zwa-workflow-timing.title: When a ZWA workflow change applies to incidents in flight
zwa-workflow-timing.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'ZWA config changes apply to the next DLP incident; in-flight incidents continue with their original workflow.' No captured ZWA source states this.

deleted-recreated-id.title: Whether a deleted resource can be restored
deleted-recreated-id.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'A deleted resource cannot be restored; recreating it gives a new resource ID, so references to the old ID need manual rewiring.' Only API clients and their secrets are captured as unrecoverable (zidentity.api-clients:delete-unrecoverable); no captured source covers ZPA, ZIA or ZCC deletions.

lss-streamed-logs.title: Whether streamed LSS logs can be recovered from Zscaler
lss-streamed-logs.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Once LSS log data is streamed it is gone: the receiving SIEM has it, and Zscaler keeps no duplicate.' No captured source addresses retention of streamed log copies.

dlp-blocked-content.title: Whether blocked DLP content is delivered when its rule is reverted
dlp-blocked-content.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'DLP-blocked content did not reach its destination, and reverting the rule does not deliver it.' No captured source states this consequence.

deception-rollback.title: Whether Deception has a configuration rollback path
deception-rollback.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Deception, Risk360, AI Security beyond AI Guard and ZMS have no verified SDK or Terraform configuration rollback path.' Risk360 is covered by risk360.overview:no-client-surface and ZMS by zms.api:clients-read-only. Deception and the rest of AI Security have no captured claim.
